header.name: Human Computer Interaction
header.description: This course will provide a detailed understanding of the fundamentals of human computer interaction including concepts of the user centered design, modern user interfaces, rapid prototyping, usability, and user evaluations.

outcomes.label: CO1
outcomes.raw_text: Have a broad understanding of human computer interaction and latest technologies. Have understanding of perceptual and cognitive basis of human-computer interaction.

outcomes.label: CO2
outcomes.raw_text: Knowledge of user centered design and techniques for rapid prototyping.

outcomes.label: CO3
outcomes.raw_text: Knowledge of evaluating multiple interface alternatives,

outcomes.label: CO4
outcomes.raw_text: Using statistics to analyze data, preparing report to visually present the insights.

lecture_topics: Introduction (History) to HCI and Interaction Design Process
Usability Testing Methods (Fitt's Law, Heuristics etc.)

weekly_plan.tutorial_assignment: Statistics for HCI Tutorial using SPSS
Statistics for HCI Tutorial using SPSS

resources.title: Human Computer Inreraction: An Empirical Research Perspective by I. Schott Mackenzie, (Morgan Kaufmann)
Research Methods in Human-Computer Interaction, by Jonathan Lazar, Jinjuan Heidi Feng, Harry Hochheiser, (Wiley)
3D User Interfaces: Theory and Practice (2nd Edition) (Usability) by Joseph J. LaViola Jr., Ernst Kruijff, Ryan P. McMahan, Doug Bowman, Ivan P. Poupyrev
Interaction Design: Beyond Human-Computer Interaction (4th Edition) by Jenny Preece, Helen Sharp, Yvonne Rogers (Wiley)
